questions.stem: Peripheral chemoreceptors respond to hypoxia using which channel?
questions.solutionHtml:
Potassium channel
  • Peripheral chemoreceptors respond to hypoxia using the C. Potassium channel.
  • Type I glomus cells (carotid and aortic body) have O2-sensitive K+ channels, whose conductance is reduced in proportion to the degree of hypoxia.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no. 648.

questions.stem: Vasopressin acts through which channels in collecting duct?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aquaporin 2
  • The antidiuretic hormone acts through aquaporin channel 2.
  • ADH binds to V2 receptors in the late distal tubules, collecting tubules, and collecting ducts, and stimulates the movement of an intracellular protein, called aquaporin-2 (AQP-2), to the luminal side of the cell membranes.


Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 364.

Tension

The Golgi tendon organ (GTO) is responsible for detecting changes in muscle tension. It is a sensory receptor located within the tendons of skeletal muscles near their insertion points into bones.

questions.stem: Hormone predominately secreted after 14 days on endometrium is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Progesterone

After ovulation occurs, the ovarian follicle transforms into the corpus luteum, which secretes predominantly progesterone.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 417.

Leydig's cells.

Testosterone is primarily secreted by Leydig's cells, also known as interstitial cells, which are located in the testes of males. These cells respond to luteinizing hormone (LH) secreted by the anterior pituitary gland, and LH stimulates Leydig cells to produce and release testosterone.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no: 417.

questions.stem: With increase in age, which of the following is true for lungs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Pulmonary compliance increases

As a person ages, the pulmonary compliance of the lungs tends to increase. Pulmonary compliance refers to the ability of the lungs to stretch and expand in response to changes in pressure.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Pagé nos 628 and 629.

questions.stem: Functional residual capacity represents the volume of air remaining in lungs?
questions.solutionHtml:
After normal expiration
  • Functional residual capacity (FRC) is the volume of air that remains in the lungs after a normal, passive expiration (exhalation) when the respiratory muscles are at rest.
  • Functional Residual Capacity (FRC) is expiratory reserve volume + residual volume.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page nos 628 and 629

questions.stem: Tubuloglomerular feedback control is useful for which one of the following?
questions.solutionHtml:
GFR
  • Tubuloglomerular feedback is a mechanism that helps regulate the glomerular filtration rate (GFR) in the kidneys.
  • The GFR is the rate at which blood is filtered by the glomeruli, the tiny blood vessels in the kidneys responsible for filtering waste and excess substances from the blood to form urine.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 672.

50ml/kg

Considered polyuricifurine production is greater than 50ml/kg/day or Polyuria is excessive or an abnormally large production or passage of urine greater than 2.5 L or 3 L over 24 hours in adults.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Page no 672.

questions.stem: According to Herrington classification, the decerebrate rigidity is characterized by all except :-

options.label: A
options.text: Rigidity occurs in all the muscles of the body

options.label: B
options.text: Increase in the rate of discharge of the y efferent neuron

options.label: C
options.text: Increased excitability of the motor neuron pool

options.label: D
options.text: Decerebration produces no phenomenon akin to spinal shock

questions.answerText: Rigidity occurs in all the muscles of the body
questions.solutionHtml:
Rigidity occurs in all the muscles of the body

In decerebrate rigidity, there is rigidity in extensor muscles of all the four extremities (not all muscles of the body).



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page no. 241 and 242

Hypoparathyroidism

Calcitonin is a hormone produced by the thyroid gland. Its primary function is to lower blood calcium levels by inhibiting the release of calcium from bones and enhancing calcium excretion by the kidneys.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Pagè nos 206, 344 and 345.

VIP
  • VIP is responsible for anterograde dilatation of the small intestine.
  • Peristalsis involves the contraction of a segment of intestine behind the bolus of food and relaxation of a segment of the intestine in front of the bolus of food.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition Pagé no: 485.

Increased heart rate

Reflex responsible for tachycardia during right atrial distension is the Bainbridge reflex.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 223.

options.label: C
options.text: As a combined entity with insulin after secretion

questions.solutionHtml:
In Proinsulin
  • C-peptide is a fragment of proinsulin, a precursor molecule of insulin.
  • Proinsulin consists of three parts: an A-chain, a B-chain, and a connecting peptide called C-peptide. After proinsulin is synthesized, it undergoes further processing to remove the C-peptide, and the remaining A and B chains combine to form the active insulin molecule.


Goodman & Gillman's The Pharmacological Basis Of Therapeutics - 13th Edition Page no: 873, Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 20th Edition Page no: 2864.

questions.stem: In a 50-year-old patient with respiratory distress, FEV1 = 1.5litre and FVC =3.5 litres. The type of disease he is suffering from:
questions.solutionHtml:
Obstructive Lung disease
  • FEV1/FVC = 1.5 liters / 3.5 liters ≈ 0.43
  • Since the FEV1/FVC ratio is significantly lower than 0.7 to 0.8, it indicates an obstructive lung disease.
  • In obstructive lung diseases, the airways are narrowed, making it difficult for the person to exhale air effectively, leading to decreased FEV1/FVC ratio. Therefore, the correct answer is: B. Obstructive Lung disease.


Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 21st Edition Pg no 2152.

questions.stem: During Exercise rapid breathing possible by which centre:
questions.solutionHtml:
VRG

During exercise, rapid breathing is possible due to activation of the VRG (Ventral Respiratory Group) in the medulla oblongata of the brainstem.



Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology, 25th Edition Pagé no: 656.

questions.stem: Slow Conduction velocity is seen with which of the following nerve fibres?
questions.solutionHtml:
Postganglionic sympathetic nerve fibres
  • Slow conduction velocity is seen with: B. Postganglionic sympathetic nerve fibers.
  • Postganglionic sympathetic (type C) has the least conduction velocity among the given options.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page no 94.

Carbon dioxide

Respiratory centers, specifically the central chemoreceptors in the medulla oblongata, are primarily stimulated by changes in the levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) in the blood.



Guyton and Hall Textbook of Medical Physiology, 13th Edition Page no 223.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true for decorticate rigidity?

options.label: A
options.text: It is produced by the removal of cerebral cortex and basal ganglia

options.label: B
options.text: Flexion of lower limbs and extension of upper limbs occurs

options.label: D
options.text: It is characterized by flexion of upper limbs and extension of lower limbs

questions.answerText: It is characterized by flexion of upper limbs and extension of lower limbs
questions.solutionHtml:
It is characterized by flexion of upper limbs and extension of lower limbs
  • Removal of the cerebral cortex (decortication) produces decorticate rigidity.
  • Characterized by flexion of the upper extremities at the elbow and extensor hyperactivity in the lower extremities.
  • The flexion can be explained by active rubrospinal excitation of flexor muscles in the upper extremities; the hyperextension of lower extremities is due to the same changes that occur after midcollicular decerebration.


Ganong's Review Of Medical Physiology - 25th Edition Page no 243
